suggestions.quote: Theo, camera up: "One question. Say you'd been minus one at midnight." "Theo." "Minus two. Minus four. Day thirty-one you owe a billion. Day forty-nine, you owe the planet." On the wall: DAY 50. 0.
suggestions.fix: Theo, camera up: "One question. Say you'd been minus one at midnight." "Theo." "Minus two. Minus four. Day thirty-one you owe a billion. Day fifty, you owe the planet." On the wall: DAY 50. 0.

suggestions.quote: Day forty-nine, morning: $281 trillion. Mr. Halloran, second call, very quiet: "Sir. At midnight your balance will be bigger than every debt on Earth put together." Every debt on Earth: more than $365 trillion (c02). At midnight you'd have $563 trillion.
suggestions.fix: Day forty-nine, morning: about $281.5 trillion. Mr. Halloran, second call, very quiet: "Sir. At midnight your balance will be bigger than every debt on Earth put together." Every debt on Earth: surpassed $365 trillion (c02). At midnight you'd have about $563 trillion.

suggestions.quote: 3. Why not spend it abroad, or on gold? Answered at 5:25: wherever you spend, that market's price breaks first; Mansa Musa did it with gold in Cairo.
suggestions.fix: 3. Why not spend it abroad, or on gold? Answered at 5:25: wherever you spend, that market's price breaks first (c10); Mansa Musa did it with gold in Cairo (c11).

keep.quote: Whatever is in your bank account at midnight is doubled by morning, starting from the one-dollar coin your grandmother sends you on your birthday, and it will not stop: in a month it buys the pier you live on, by day forty-eight it is bigger than everything the whole world makes in a year (about $128 trillion, the IMF's 2026 projection; claims.md c01), and by day fifty-eight it overflows the number box most computers count in (c06).
"Most money, sir, is made when a bank lends. And when a loan is repaid, the money doesn't go anywhere. It stops existing. The Bank of England wrote that down in 2014." (c03, c04)
"On most computer systems, the number box is sixty-four bits. And because the bank counts in cents, day fifty-eight overflows into a negative nineteen-digit number (c06)."
